title: Recording: Loup (1st Indian On The Moon) by Wings | 1972
content:
Studio One, Olympic Studios, London
Producer: Glyn Johns
Engineer: Phil Chapman

Wings began recording ‘Loup (1st Indian On The Moon)’ for their second album Red Rose Speedway on 15 March 1972.

The song was recorded over three consecutive days at Olympic Studios in Barnes, London.

I love it, although it’s really not a commercial track at all. It’s a moody instrumental. It’s just a thing really, hard to explain about the first Red Indian on the Moon called Loup. It’s just a story but you can see through his eyes. It’s a spacey track, but the album’s not like that.
Paul McCartney, 2018
Melody Maker, 2 December 1972

A new instrument was brought to the studio for this session: Linda McCartney’s Minimoog Model D synthesizer. The other members of Wings were eager to try out its new sounds, and began jamming what became ‘Loup (1st Indian On The Moon)’.
